exclude: Resident code, cached duplicate, output and machine memory outside this overlay
extra: Complete2048-byte loaded level file, including retained previous-file tails

comments.text: Two inverse screen-code digits copied into the status display; Mystery Maze file variants share number25.
Initial placement-stream pointer consumed by resident $7514/$4D0F before the private initialization callback.
Background and border color bytes. Loader uses pristine backup $3804/$3805 when publishing VIC colors.
Seven-byte bomb record pointer. The scanner searches for key $FF; target count $3013 need not equal record count. PLF13 uniquely omits the terminator after its four intended records.
Four pending callback pointers copied by $758A into $40C8-$40CF. A zero high byte leaves the existing no-op task; nonzero vectors are committed by the resident IRQ.
Initial player X low, X high and Y in hardware sprite coordinates, read by spawn $56E0. This is the start of each life, not multicolor drawing coordinates.
Initial target counter 12. Collection decrements it; special bomb callbacks can compensate the decrement or replace the table. Primary record list has 12 entries.
Resident perimeter-bullet slot limit 0; $6800 considers sprite slots1 through limit-minus-one. Private level actors can use other slots.
Ordinary collection adds this little-endian binary value (100) to the24-bit total score. Private callbacks may add an extra award first.
Initial little-endian bonus 1500. The resident countdown subtracts100 per256 enabled IRQ services; completion adds the remaining amount to total and bonus records.
Private initialization routine called after initial scenery drawing. Common no-op target is the RTS at $301F.
Main-thread entry selected by JMP($301B) at $759C; typically the spawn/collection/exit loop at $3050.
Private cleanup hook copied into the local JSR trampoline before completion or exhaustion. A target of $301F returns immediately.
Shared one-byte RTS used by empty initialization, cleanup and individual bomb callbacks in this overlay.
Eight ladder/up-rope X columns followed by six down-rope X columns, copied to $40B0-$40BD. Coordinates use160-wide multicolor space; $FF marks unavailable columns.
Two zero header bytes between the climb-column arrays and completion vector; the shared loader does not read them as part of those arrays.
Ordinary successful-level destination $5B00. The private loop calls cleanup before jumping through this word.
Exhausted-lives destination $5FFD, the resident jump to game-over presentation $6A80. This is separate from successful completion.
Two filename suffix characters '03'. Resident loader copies them into $40D3/$40D4; private cleanup can replace them before the next disk request.
Single $FF drawing-stream terminator, used as the no-change post-bomb action.
Zero byte after the empty drawing terminator and before collection-key coordinate offsets.
X/Y offsets applied by resident $55BF when reducing player position to the bomb lookup key. They adjust the coarse cell test, not the visible bomb positions.
Optional hook called before the matched bomb-record callback. A zero high byte suppresses the call; otherwise the resident patches JSR $5643 from this word.
Twenty loaded zero bytes align the private main loop to $3050. Header fields end at $303B; no private structure is assigned to this gap.

Spawn/reveal a life through $436A, then repeatedly check bomb collection through $436D. Zero remaining count at $3013 exits through success vector $3030 after setting divisor 9; death state $4028=2 waits for state 0, then respawns unless lives sentinel $40E4=$FF, which exits through $3032. Both exits call the header cleanup pointer.

Patch local JSR operand from little-endian header $301D/$301E, invoke cleanup, return. In this file the header resolves to shared no-op RTS at $301F; the assembled $FFFF target is a placeholder, not a real call.

Drawing data $308F-$3119 read by Initial scenery $308F. Stream commands are FE shape pointer, FD repeat delta, FC stream jump, x/y/count placement and FF end. Referenced shapes hold width/x-offset/y-offset/pixel rows endingFF; source pixel codes are0 background,1 bomb,2 support,3 climbable. Parsed by the same behavioral renderer checked against original $4D0F.

12 seven-byte records [coarse key,x,y,callback low/high,post-draw low/high]. Terminator: $FF. Coordinates are160-wide bitmap positions. The resident scanner matches the key, calls both hooks, adds $3015 points, erases the bomb, follows the draw pointer and decrements $3013. This list is not bounded by the target counter.
Fourth IRQ callback requests death 1 if phase $402B is nonzero, state $4028 is 0 and player collision shadow $4088 is nonzero.

Thirty three-byte records for sprite 7, initially waiting for a collected bomb. Ordinary record=(motion index 0..6,duration,unused 0); FE waits for global bomb flag; FF followed by a little-endian address loops back to $3184.
Twenty-three three-byte records for sprite 6. FE gates segments on a bomb collection event, ordinary indices select signed velocity/frame lookup, and final FF,$31DE restarts this route.

Expand compact graphics from $3345 through $4376; place sprites 6/7 at (120,152)/(232,216), X-high 0, frame $10 and enabled state $10. Set individual colours 3 and 5. Velocity/countdown/pointer state is supplied by overlay data.
Global bomb callback: increment event $3336. Live first pickup awards100, targets12 to11, then releases both robots on the next eligible shared update. CPU checks execute the full original collector.

Update robot7 then6 on a hazard pulse unless death mode2; after both, clear shared bomb event at $3275. Both waiting robots see the same event. An event received while both are moving is discarded rather than queued. CPU checked all53 triples over2400 updates; live first release moves7 to236,216 and6 to116,152. Position deltas use signed16-bit X and8-bit Y; decrement segment duration and set frame base plus phase$4024.

Read script pointer from split arrays $3341-$3344. Ordinary first byte indexes seven-element dx-low/dx-high/dy/frame arrays; second is countdown. Play step cue $33F9, advance pointer 3 and immediately update motion. FE/FF dispatch to wait/jump handlers.
FF command reads next two script bytes as little-endian target, stores the actor split pointer and immediately decodes there; both authored routes loop within their own streams.
FE command holds the robot at base frame $10 OR $4024 while event $3336 is zero. Nonzero event advances past this three-byte wait without consuming the event until both actors finish.
Seven horizontal delta low bytes:0,4,0,FC,FC,4,FC, paired with high bytes at $3321.
Seven horizontal delta high bytes 0,0,0,FF,FF,0,FF; combine with $331A to encode 0,+4,0,-4,-4,+4,-4.
Seven vertical deltas FE,0,2,0,1,1,FF for up, horizontal, down and diagonal motions.
Seven frame bases 10,12,10,14,14,12,14; add shared phase $4024 to alternate one of three two-frame direction pairs.

Bomb event byte followed by seven two-byte arrays: countdowns, dx-low, dx-high, dy, framebase, script-low and script-high. Initial sprite 6 pointer=$31DE, sprite 7=$3184; both countdowns and deltas start 0.

Six authored compact 30-byte sprite frames (24 x 10 pixels). $4376 expands to 64-byte slots $8400-$857F used by bases $10/$12/$14. Loader always reads eight chunks, so its final 60 bytes come from following routine/sound/fill and occupy unused slots $16/$17.
Save actor X at $3413, queue $3414 with priority 4, release 0 and pulse control $40, then restore X so motion-script decoding can continue.
Actor loop X saved across the shared sound allocator by $33F9.
Sound envelope 00/22 and pulse-width 8888, followed by frequencies 0868,10CF,219F,4D3D held 2 ticks each, terminated 0. This rising cue starts each movement segment.

Loaded patterned residue after the terminated sound stream. Entire range is byte-identical to PLF01 and PLF04 tails. The graphics loader overreads $3427-$3434 into an unused frame slot; no active robot frame or execution target uses it.
